/-!
# Convergence of the Flint Hills and Cookson Hills series

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Examples of numerical series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Series_(mathematics)#Examples_of_numerical_series)
- [MathWorld: Flint Hills Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/FlintHillsSeries.html)
- [Alekseyev, On the Flint Hills series](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1104.5100)
- [MathWorld: Cookson Hills Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/CooksonHillsSeries.html)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace FlintCooksonHills

/--
The Flint Hills series summing $csc(n)^2 / n^3$ from $n=1$ to $\infty$ converges.
(Note that we 0-index the series below.)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 40]
theorem flint_hills_series_converges :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      Summable (fun n : ℕ =>
        1 / ((((n + 1) : ℝ)^3) * (Real.sin (n + 1)^2))) := by
  sorry

/--
The Cookson Hills series summing $sec(n)^2 / n^3$ from $n=1$ to $\infty$ converges.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 40]
theorem cookson_hills_series_converges :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      Summable (fun n : ℕ =>
        1 / ((((n + 1) : ℝ)^3) * (Real.cos (n + 1)^2))) := by
  sorry

end FlintCooksonHills

reformulations.difference: Lean uses unconditional Summable on the zero-indexed sequence 1/((n+1)^3·sin(n+1)^2), whereas the source asks about ordinary convergence of the series starting at 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All terms are nonnegative, so hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat_of_nonneg identifies unconditional summability with existence of a finite real limit of the ordinary partial sums. Reindexing by n+1 gives exactly the source's partial sums over 1 ≤ n ≤ N. This equivalence was proved as Review.flint_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using either admitted conjecture.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses unconditional Summable on the zero-indexed sequence 1/((n+1)^3·cos(n+1)^2), whereas the source asks about ordinary convergence of the series starting at 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The reciprocal-square expression equals sec(n+1)^2/(n+1)^3 and is nonnegative. Thus unconditional summability is equivalent to convergence of ordinary partial sums; the index shift gives exactly the source's sums over 1 ≤ n ≤ N. This equivalence was proved as Review.cookson_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using either admitted conjecture.

sources_consulted: Max A. Alekseyev, On convergence of the Flint Hills series (2011), arXiv:1104.5100v1; full LaTeX source obtained from https://arxiv.org/e-print/1104.5100
review.notes: Both declarations were checked. Scratch proofs also establish strict positivity of every denominator, excluding any division-by-zero default-value issue, and verify the first terms. The scratch file compiles successfully; the equivalence and denominator proofs have no sorryAx dependency. The cited sources still describe both convergence questions as open. The newer claimed Flint Hills proof linked by MathWorld, arXiv:2502.03474, was withdrawn on 14 September 2026 with an explicit acknowledgment that convergence was not proved; it does not warrant a status change.
